research_question: What is the effect of extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) compared with retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) on treatment success at three months in adults with kidney stones?
outcome_description: Treatment success (stone-free or absence of clinically significant residual fragments, as defined by trial imaging) at approximately three months follow-up, analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis.
positive_direction: Higher treatment success rate favoring ESWL over RIRS (RR > 1 favors ESWL; RR < 1 favors RIRS)
search_queries: extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy retrograde intrarenal surgery renal stones randomized trial
ESWL RIRS kidney stones stone free rate trial
shock wave lithotripsy flexible ureteroscopy renal calculi comparison trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials comparing extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL/SWL) with retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS/flexible ureteroscopy)
Adult participants diagnosed with renal (kidney) calculi
Reporting quantitative data on treatment success or stone-free rates at or near three-month follow-up
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and narrative reviews are excluded)
No direct comparison between ESWL and RIRS (e.g., comparisons solely between ESWL and PCNL, or studies evaluating ureteral calculi rather than renal stones)
No quantitative outcome data reported that permits calculation of treatment success or stone-free rates
Studies conducted exclusively in pediatric populations (<18 years of age) or completely unrelated topics
moderators_to_extract: Stone size or stone burden (mm or surface area)
Stone location (e.g., lower pole vs. non-lower pole)
Definition of treatment success (complete stone clearance vs. residual fragments <=4 mm)
Imaging modality used to assess stone-free status (CT, KUB radiography, ultrasound)
Actual follow-up timepoint of assessment (e.g., 1, 3, or 6 months)
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) of treatment success calculated as ESWL divided by RIRS; RR < 1 favors RIRS, and RR > 1 favors ESWL.
